columns.justification: Dump artifact (measured unique), used as the conversion's unique key and last sort column because tr_job_id is not unique in this release. Identifier — not a model feature.
columns.meaning: Row number of the job row in the dump; documented as the unique identifier of a build job.
columns.name: row

columns.justification: Known at trigger time. Identifier — not a model feature.
columns.meaning: SHA-1 of the commit that triggered the build.
columns.name: git_commit

columns.justification: Known before the build. Identifier — not a model feature.
columns.meaning: GitHub repository name (owner/repo).
columns.name: gh_project_name

columns.justification: Property of the trigger event.
columns.meaning: Whether the build was triggered as part of a pull request.
columns.name: gh_is_pr

columns.justification: Describes how the PR was eventually merged, which can happen after the build — possible future information.
columns.meaning: For PR builds: how the pull request was merged. The page calls it the SHA-1 of the merging commit, but the values are a few categorical codes (see Distinct).
columns.name: git_merged_with

columns.justification: Repository metadata, used to select the Java subset. Context — not a model feature.
columns.meaning: Dominant repository language according to GitHub (partition key).
columns.name: gh_lang

columns.justification: Known at trigger time. Context — not a model feature.
columns.meaning: Branch git_commit was committed on.
columns.name: git_branch

columns.justification: Carries no information beyond tr_started_at and is not UTC (measured, see evidence): never use it as a commit time or a feature.
columns.meaning: Documented as the timestamp of the first commit in the triggering push (the 2016-07-28 page version: first commit of the whole repository). Measured: a copy of tr_started_at in UK local time (GMT/BST), not a commit timestamp (see evidence).
columns.name: gh_first_commit_created_at

columns.justification: The later page bounds it to the window ending at the trigger; the earlier page does not state a window.
columns.meaning: Developers who committed directly or merged PRs in the 3 months up to the build trigger (the 2016-07-28 page version: size of the team, no window).
columns.name: gh_team_size

columns.justification: List of commit SHAs that exist before the build. Identifier — not a model feature.
columns.meaning: Commits of the triggering push minus the built commit, '#'-separated (the 2016-07-28 page version: directly preceding commits without their own build).
columns.name: git_commits

columns.justification: Computed from the commits being built, which exist before the build starts.
columns.meaning: Number of entries in git_commits.
columns.name: git_num_commits

columns.justification: Not time-bounded to the build start in the docs; may count comments written after the build — possible future information.
columns.meaning: If git_commit is linked to a PR: number of discussion comments on that PR.
columns.name: gh_num_issue_comments

columns.justification: Not time-bounded to the build start in the docs; may count comments written after the build — possible future information.
columns.meaning: Number of GitHub comments on the built commits.
columns.name: gh_num_commit_comments

columns.justification: Not time-bounded to the build start in the docs; may count review comments written after the build — possible future information.
columns.meaning: For PR builds: number of code-review comments on the pull request.
columns.name: gh_num_pr_comments

columns.justification: Computed from the commits being built, which exist before the build starts.
columns.meaning: Lines of production code changed by the commits built by this build (the 2016-07-28 page version: churn of git_commit only).
columns.name: gh_src_churn

columns.justification: Computed from the commits being built, which exist before the build starts.
columns.meaning: Lines of test code changed by the commits built by this build (the 2016-07-28 page version: churn of git_commit only).
columns.name: gh_test_churn

columns.justification: Computed from the commits being built, which exist before the build starts.
columns.meaning: Files added by the commits built by this build.
columns.name: gh_files_added

columns.justification: Computed from the commits being built, which exist before the build starts.
columns.meaning: Files deleted by the commits built by this build.
columns.name: gh_files_deleted

columns.justification: Computed from the commits being built, which exist before the build starts.
columns.meaning: Files modified by the commits built by this build.
columns.name: gh_files_modified

columns.justification: Computed from the commits being built, which exist before the build starts.
columns.meaning: Tests added by the built commits: lines of test code per the later page, test cases (e.g. @Test annotations) per the 2016-07-28 page version (see evidence).
columns.name: gh_tests_added

columns.justification: Computed from the commits being built, which exist before the build starts.
columns.meaning: Tests deleted by the built commits (same two definitions as gh_tests_added).
columns.name: gh_tests_deleted

columns.justification: Computed from the commits being built, which exist before the build starts.
columns.meaning: Production source files changed by the built commits (the 2016-07-28 page version: production files in the whole repository; see evidence).
columns.name: gh_src_files

columns.justification: Computed from the commits being built, which exist before the build starts.
columns.meaning: Documentation files changed by the built commits (the 2016-07-28 page version: documentation files in the repository).
columns.name: gh_doc_files

columns.justification: Computed from the commits being built, which exist before the build starts.
columns.meaning: Changed files that are neither production code nor documentation (the 2016-07-28 page version: such files in the repository).
columns.name: gh_other_files

columns.justification: Counts commits that precede the trigger under either page version.
columns.meaning: Distinct commits in the 3 months up to the trigger that touched the files changed by the built commits (the 2016-07-28 page version: all earlier commits on those files, no window).
columns.name: gh_commits_on_files_touched

columns.justification: Repository state at the built commit.
columns.meaning: Executable production source lines in the whole repository (comments excluded).
columns.name: gh_sloc

columns.justification: Repository state at the built commit.
columns.meaning: Test density: lines of test code per 1,000 gh_sloc.
columns.name: gh_test_lines_per_kloc

columns.justification: Repository state at the built commit.
columns.meaning: Test density: test cases per 1,000 gh_sloc.
columns.name: gh_test_cases_per_kloc

columns.justification: Repository state at the built commit.
columns.meaning: Assert density: assertions per 1,000 gh_sloc.
columns.name: gh_asserts_cases_per_kloc

columns.justification: Property of the commit author before the build.
columns.meaning: Whether the built commit was authored by a core team member.
columns.name: gh_by_core_team_member

columns.justification: Taken from the final PR text, which can be edited after the build (ADR-0017 context) — possible future information.
columns.meaning: For PR builds: total words in the pull request title and description.
columns.name: gh_description_complexity

columns.justification: Assigned when the build is created. Identifier — not a model feature.
columns.meaning: Travis CI build id.
columns.name: tr_build_id

columns.justification: Known at trigger time. Identifier — not a model feature.
columns.meaning: For PR builds: the pull request number on GitHub.
columns.name: gh_pull_req_num

columns.justification: The prediction target (ADR-0005); only known once the build finished.
columns.meaning: Build status from the Travis API (passed, failed, errored, canceled, started).
columns.name: tr_status

columns.justification: Only known once the build finished; usable only as lagged history of finished builds.
columns.meaning: Overall build duration reported by Travis, in seconds (summed job time per DATASET_AUDIT §4.1, so started_at + duration only bounds the finish time).
columns.name: tr_duration

columns.justification: Trigger time; used for ordering, history windows and time features. Caveat: a restart overwrites it (DATASET_AUDIT §4.3).
columns.meaning: Start of the build process (UTC wall-clock, verified against the secondary archive; see evidence).
columns.name: tr_started_at

columns.justification: Jobs are created together with the build (the matrix is known at creation). Identifier — not a model feature.
columns.meaning: Travis job ids of the build, as a bracketed comma-separated list ('[id, id, ...]').
columns.name: tr_jobs

columns.justification: Assigned when the build is created. Identifier — not a model feature.
columns.meaning: Per-project serial build number on Travis.
columns.name: tr_build_number

columns.justification: Assigned when the build's jobs are created. Identifier — not a model feature.
columns.meaning: Travis job id of this row; documented as one of tr_jobs (not always true, see invariants).
columns.name: tr_job_id

columns.justification: Derived from the build log (formally post-build) while the language itself is a repository property already given by gh_lang; tagged uncertain. Identifier — not a model feature.
columns.meaning: Language of the build as recognised by the build-log analyzer.
columns.name: tr_lan

columns.justification: Produced by analysing the finished build's log; forbidden for the current build.
columns.meaning: Setup time before the Travis build started, in seconds.
columns.name: tr_setup_time

columns.justification: Produced by analysing the finished build's log; forbidden for the current build.
columns.meaning: Build-log analyzer that processed the log (e.g. java-ant, java-maven, java-gradle).
columns.name: tr_analyzer

columns.justification: Produced by analysing the finished build's log; forbidden for the current build.
columns.meaning: Test frameworks the analyzer recognised, '#'-separated.
columns.name: tr_frameworks

columns.justification: Produced by analysing the finished build's log; forbidden for the current build.
columns.meaning: Number of passed tests, if the analyzer could tell.
columns.name: tr_tests_ok

columns.justification: Produced by analysing the finished build's log; forbidden for the current build.
columns.meaning: Number of failed tests, if the analyzer could tell.
columns.name: tr_tests_fail

columns.justification: Produced by analysing the finished build's log; forbidden for the current build.
columns.meaning: Number of tests run, if the analyzer could tell.
columns.name: tr_tests_run

columns.justification: Produced by analysing the finished build's log; forbidden for the current build.
columns.meaning: Number of skipped or ignored tests, if the analyzer could tell.
columns.name: tr_tests_skipped

columns.justification: Produced by analysing the finished build's log; forbidden for the current build.
columns.meaning: Names of the failed tests, '#'-separated (free text).
columns.name: tr_failed_tests

columns.justification: Produced by analysing the finished build's log; forbidden for the current build.
columns.meaning: Seconds spent running the tests.
columns.name: tr_testduration

columns.justification: Produced by analysing the finished build's log; forbidden for the current build.
columns.meaning: Seconds the build itself ran, without Travis scheduling and provisioning.
columns.name: tr_purebuildduration

columns.justification: Produced by analysing the finished build's log; forbidden for the current build.
columns.meaning: Whether tests ran in this job.
columns.name: tr_tests_ran

columns.justification: Produced by analysing the finished build's log; forbidden for the current build.
columns.meaning: Whether tests failed in this job.
columns.name: tr_tests_failed

columns.justification: Measured to be bounded by git_num_commits + 1 (evidence), i.e. committers of commits that exist before the build; the page's project-wide wording is not time-bounded, so verify before relying on it.
columns.meaning: Documented as the number of people who committed to the project; measured to count the committers of the built commits (see evidence).
columns.name: git_num_committers

columns.justification: The build matrix is known when the build is created.
columns.meaning: Number of jobs of the build (length of tr_jobs).
columns.name: tr_num_jobs

columns.justification: Linkage to an earlier build: its id is known at trigger time, but that build's outcome may not be (use the finished-before rule). -1 is a placeholder that staging turns into NULL. Identifier — not a model feature.
columns.meaning: Link to the previous build, given as its tr_build_id; -1 (also written -1.0) when there is none. Measured to differ between jobs of the same build.
columns.name: tr_prev_build

columns.justification: Only observable once Travis picked the build up, i.e. after the trigger moment.
columns.meaning: Latency induced by Travis (scheduling, build pick-up), in seconds; -1 placeholder.
columns.name: tr_ci_latency

dataformat_doc.note: Last page version describing this 56-column format (2016-11-09). The first version (commit 1ca2ce08d42e, 2016-07-28) defines gh_first_commit_created_at, gh_team_size, git_commits, the comment counts, the change columns, gh_tests_added/deleted, gh_src/doc/other_files, gh_commits_on_files_touched and gh_description_complexity differently. Both post-date the dump (dated 2016-03-05 by its file name); measured evidence below decides where possible.

dataset.attribution: Beller, M., Gousios, G., Zaidman, A. TravisTorrent: Synthesizing Travis CI and GitHub for Full-Stack Research on Continuous Integration. MSR 2017, DOI 10.1109/MSR.2017.24. Data: Figshare DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.19314170 (CC BY 4.0).
dataset.timestamp_semantics: TIMESTAMP (no zone). tr_started_at is UTC wall-clock (measured: equal to the secondary archive's explicit-UTC started_at on every joined build). gh_first_commit_created_at is tr_started_at rendered in Europe/London local time (measured), i.e. not UTC.
dataset.title: TravisTorrent (Figshare `travistorrent_5_3_2016`)

duplicate_job_rows.method: Java job rows grouped by tr_job_id; 'listed' = the job id appears in the row's own tr_jobs

file_count_definition.method: Java builds: src + doc + other files vs files added + deleted + modified (repository-wide counts would usually exceed the touched files)

gh_first_commit_created_at.method: Java job rows: gh_first_commit_created_at compared with tr_started_at

git_num_committers.method: Java job rows with both values

tests_added_definition.method: Java builds: if gh_tests_added/deleted were lines of test code, test churn > 0 would imply tests added or deleted > 0, and tests added could not exceed churn

build_columns_constant.note: varying: tr_build_number, git_num_committers, tr_num_jobs (at most 8,943 builds)
build_columns_constant.rule: build-grain columns are constant within a build

ci_latency_non_negative.rule: tr_ci_latency >= 0 unless it is the -1 placeholder

first_commit_before_start.note: every violation is an exact +1 h / +2 h offset (see evidence)
first_commit_before_start.rule: gh_first_commit_created_at <= tr_started_at (the first commit precedes the build)

job_id_unique.note: extra rows beyond one per distinct tr_job_id (see evidence: duplicate job rows)
job_id_unique.rule: tr_job_id is unique across job rows

job_listed_in_own_build.rule: tr_job_id is one of its build's tr_jobs

prev_build_not_earlier.note: order history by tr_started_at with the finished-before rule, not by this link
prev_build_not_earlier.rule: tr_prev_build < tr_build_id (the previous build was created earlier)

prev_build_other_non_positive.rule: tr_prev_build is > 0 unless it is the -1 placeholder

prev_build_placeholder.rule: tr_prev_build is a build id (not the -1 placeholder)

test_counts_non_negative.of_label: job rows with a test count

measurement.build_grain: one row per tr_build_id: a job row whose tr_job_id is listed in the build's own tr_jobs first, then the lowest (tr_job_id, row)
measurement.job_grain: every job row (raw is not deduplicated)
measurement.null_definition: SQL NULL after conversion (raw empty field, the 'NA' token, or a value that failed its strict cast — see Cast failures)
